markdown_report:
The best first step remains an architecture-aware, paired history-sensitivity diagnostic adapter. At 0% progress, reliable measurements provide a practical foundation for subsequent SASRec changes; the adapter itself makes no accuracy-improvement claim.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Existing margins measure sampled training separation. They cannot establish validation ranking quality. (2) Mean embedding cosine measures directional alignment. It cannot independently establish collapse or personalization. (3) Qualitative feedback suggests insufficient specificity and possible stale-history influence. These remain hypotheses because present intent, ownership and compatibility are generally unobserved.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Oh and Cho [1] motivate measuring recency dependence, without justifying increased recent-item weight. (2) Liu et al. [2] identify availability confounding; their constrained swaps require training timestamps and do not uniformly sample feasible permutations. (3) Krichene and Rendle [3] show sampled ranking can disagree with full-catalog ranking, so pinned macro validation HR@10 remains the selection criterion. (4) SASRec implementation [4] and PyTorch documentation [5] expose positional and RNG confounds that the initial adapter omitted.

**Directions and framework.** Organize diagnosis along three axes: representation behavior, ranking sensitivity, and evidence quality. Embedding probes occupy the first axis; paired perturbations connect the first two; title/description evidence constrains interpretation. Across these axes, distinguish content removal, order changes, positional changes and measurement reproducibility. The gap is a reproducible adapter connecting model behavior to testable hypotheses without inventing intent.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/implementation difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Paired history-sensitivity adapter [1,2,4,5]: 5/7/7.** Originality: useful integration, though established components. Potential: reusable across architectures, though sensitivity may not predict accuracy. Difficulty: existing hooks help, though RNG isolation, timestamp alignment and masking require substantial care.
- **Contextual-versus-pooled branch ablation [1,2]: 4/7/6.** Originality: interpretable comparison, though familiar. Potential: can motivate simpler models, though ablations require retraining confirmation. Difficulty: lightweight pooling, though architecture changes require a matching predictor writer.
- **Evidence-backed specificity audit: 6/6/5.** Originality: connects factual evidence to diagnosis, though its taxonomy is heuristic. Potential: clarifies qualitative failures, though intent remains unknown. Difficulty: uses available text, though reliable matching requires manual checks.

**Selected algorithm.** Precompute an isolated training-history diagnostic panel, capped at ten batches, with fixed users, original next-item targets and supplied negative candidates. Never consume the active training loader. For each example, perturb only its target’s preceding prefix; global input shuffling against shifted labels can expose future targets. Compare intact histories with equal-count recent, older and random deletion; repeated unrestricted and availability-constrained shuffling; and shuffling preserving the latest item.

SASRec uses right-aligned histories with left-padding and scores the final slot [4]. Keep padding and length fixed for shuffles. Compacted deletion changes context and absolute positions; add position-preserving deletion only when the architecture explicitly supports masked holes. Position-only controls require explicit position IDs. Otherwise mark these controls unavailable and report confounding.

```text
precompute isolated panel, negatives and seeded perturbations
save RNG states and module modes; enter eval/no_grad
for fixed target-prefix example:
    score intact prefix on fixed candidate pair
    score eligible perturbations on that same pair
    record margin delta, ordering flip and feature distance
aggregate draws within user, users within dataset, datasets equally
restore RNG states and module modes in finally
return metrics, metric_definitions
```

Preserve both diagnostic callables. Report counts, displacement, eligible-swap rates, signed effects and user-cluster intervals; use null for unavailable measurements. Treat training results as in-sample sensitivity, never causal preference or HR@10. Freeze panel construction, seeds and analysis before inspecting validation outcomes; otherwise label associations exploratory. Restore RNGs without assuming this rewinds workers [5], and verify subsequent training batches and updates match diagnostics-disabled execution. Keep the twenty full-catalog simulator users descriptive. Select interventions only through host-provided per-category and macro validation HR@10, retaining splits, seeds, routing and evaluation.

idea.description: Implement a paired history-sensitivity diagnostic adapter around the actual trained model, with isolated diagnostic sampling, fixed-target prefix perturbations and explicit positional controls. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics with definitions, eligible counts and limitations.
idea.motivation: The current adapter measures embedding alignment and sampled training separation but does not test how history affects ranking. Qualitative feedback motivates specificity and recency hypotheses, while the supplied implementation evidence shows that naive shuffling, deletion and training-loader iteration can introduce target leakage, positional confounding and training-state changes. This revision retains the original measurement-first direction while correcting those gaps. Its potential rating decreases from 8 to 7 because diagnostic sensitivity has no established relationship to the selection objective; implementation difficulty increases from 4 to 7 because reproducibility and architecture-specific masking are substantive requirements.
idea.implementation_notes:
Data and scope: Use only public training interaction histories, aligned timestamps, titles and descriptions. The task-specific restrictions override the generic metadata examples: ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores and simulator traits are unavailable. Keep DATA_DIR as os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all artifacts beneath the trial directory, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes and single-GPU execution. Respect the host SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Preserve official splits and the pinned evaluator. This diagnostic-only intervention needs no predictor architecture change; any later architecture intervention must update the predictor writer.

Panel construction: Retain the train_loader argument for compatibility, but never iterate or modify the active training loader, its sampler, workers, negative sampler or generators. Construct a separate deterministic panel from view.user_train using dedicated Python, NumPy and Torch generators seeded 42. For each eligible user with at least two training interactions, use the final training transition: the prefix excludes the final training item, which remains the fixed positive target. These examples are explicitly in-sample because the model trained on those interactions. Sample negatives using the baseline's training eligibility rules and a dedicated diagnostic generator, then persist their exact IDs. Configure and record a cap of ten batches and the batch size before running diagnostics; deterministically sample users if the cap binds. For per-dataset execution, persist a separate panel for each category and aggregate their results later. Never replace or repartition official training data. Persist user IDs, targets, candidates, prefix windows, timestamps, selected deletion positions, perturbation seeds and configuration so every checkpoint receives the same intervention.

Feature and target alignment: Inspect the actual hook contract during implementation. Accept B x L x D sequence features or a documented final-feature output, and reject unexpected shapes rather than broadcasting silently. For baseline SASRec, truncate oldest interactions, right-align retained items, left-pad with ID 0, retain absolute slot positions and score the final slot. Do not renumber real-item positions from zero. For any per-position diagnostic extension, construct each target's preceding prefix independently and freeze its original target; never globally shuffle an input sequence while retaining its shifted training labels. Historical repeats of the target that already precede the prediction point remain legitimate history.

Perturbations: For retained prefix length n >= 2, set deletion count k = max(1, floor(0.25*n)), capped at n-1. Remove the newest k items, oldest k items, or a seeded uniformly sampled k-position subset. Preserve order among survivors and compact using baseline left-padding. These comparisons jointly change content, context and some absolute positions. A separate position-preserving deletion control must keep surviving items in their original slots, explicitly mask holes as keys and states, and gather the newest surviving feature when the final slot is removed. Enable this only through an architecture adapter that verifies mask behavior; zero IDs alone are insufficient evidence. Position-only controls require an explicit position-ID interface with unchanged content and masks. Mark unsupported controls null with a reason. Run five persisted perturbation draws with local seeds 42 through 46. Shuffle only nonpadding slots, preserving multiplicities, timestamps as slots, targets and candidate IDs; include a separate condition that preserves the latest item.

Availability-constrained shuffling: Compute item minimum timestamps across complete public training histories before window truncation. Preserve event/timestamp alignment and timestamp ties. Following the supplied description of Liu et al.'s author implementation, freeze every occurrence whose timestamp equals its item's training minimum. Scan positions chronologically; at each unfrozen i, choose uniformly among unfrozen j >= i satisfying first(item_j) <= timestamp_i and first(item_i) <= timestamp_j, and swap item IDs. Self-swaps are allowed. For the latest-item-preserving variant, exclude that position from both swap roles. Use dedicated seeded randomness rather than the author's unseeded global Python RNG. Apply swaps within retained windows and explicitly identify this as a window-restricted adaptation, not an exact reproduction of complete-history shuffling. Report displaced-occurrence fraction, eligible partner counts and nonself-swap rate; repeated items can make performed swaps observationally unchanged. Missing or inconsistent timestamps make this condition unavailable. Training first observations approximate availability, can overconstrain permutations, and do not establish release dates or causal behavioral effects.

State isolation: Use view.model, the actual nn.Module. Save each module's training flag, Python/NumPy/Torch CPU/CUDA RNG states and relevant explicit-generator states, then restore them in try/finally. Use eval and no_grad, preserve heterogeneous module modes, and verify no forward hook mutates buffers. Torch fork_rng alone does not cover Python, NumPy or workers. Parent RNG restoration cannot rewind prefetched training batches, so independent diagnostic workers and samplers are mandatory; preferably use precomputed tensors without workers. Verify enabled versus disabled diagnostics from the same initial checkpoint and RNG state produce identical subsequent training batches, negatives and parameter updates under the existing determinism guarantees. Charge verification and diagnostic computation to the shared GPU budget.

Measurements: Retain mean off-diagonal normalized item-embedding cosine over up to 2,048 nonpadding items sampled with an isolated seed-42 generator, but name it alignment rather than established collapse. Its transformed value (cosine+1)/2 is approximately 0.5 for zero mean cosine. Retain intact positive-minus-negative mean, tenth percentile, fraction below zero and fraction below 0.5, explicitly labeling them sampled in-sample statistics. For perturbations, report perturbed-minus-intact margin, ordering-flip fraction and cosine distance between final features, excluding zero-norm features. Define pair ordering by margin > 0 and report ties separately. Preserve fixed candidates and original targets across every paired comparison. Use null plus an explanation for empty or unsupported measurements; omit unavailable category/review breakdowns. Do not interpret two-candidate statistics as HR@10. Optional target-rank changes and top-10 overlap require a separately fixed, larger candidate set and a declared tie rule; full-catalog diagnostics additionally fix unseen-item eligibility from the original history rather than the perturbed history.

Aggregation and calibration: Average repeated draws within each user, then users within each dataset, then the four dataset means equally. Report category results, eligible-user counts and coverage alongside the macro result. For checkpoint comparisons, use common eligible users and resample each user's entire checkpoint trajectory together within its category; compute 1,000 seeded user-cluster bootstrap replicates and percentile 95% intervals when sample size permits. These intervals are conditional on the fixed panel, candidates and fitted models and exclude training-seed variability and search bias. Freeze diagnostic configuration and checkpoint schedule before inspecting benchmark outcomes. Thresholds, if needed, require training-history-only internal calibration without altering official splits; otherwise make no threshold claims. Correlations across shared-user checkpoints are exploratory unless their dependence is explicitly modeled, and cannot demonstrate causality. Never optimize for large perturbation effects or small embedding cosine: either can reward shortcuts rather than relevance. Benchmark selection remains the host's 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42 and equal-weight macro HR@10. Keep the twenty simulator users' full-catalog lists qualitative, reporting unseen filtering, coverage, popularity concentration and evidence-backed title observations without inferring satisfaction or latent traits.

Interpretation: diagnosis_interpreter_prompt must embed both measured metrics and metric_definitions, including counts, intervention scope and unavailable conditions. Require status, core_findings, key_implications and evidence, and prohibit invented intent, causal preference claims and unsupported compatibility conclusions. Distinguish documented prerequisites from unknown user equipment, possible redundancy from established ownership, and specific media matches from present desirability. No empirical validation gains are claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def __init__(self, view, device):
        self.view, self.device = view, device
        # Lazily load or construct a persisted diagnostic panel independently
        # of every training sampler, worker and negative-sampling stream.

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        # Signature retained; do not iterate the active training loader.
        state = capture_all_rng_states_and_per_module_modes(self.view.model)
        try:
            panel = load_or_build_isolated_training_panel(
                self.view.user_train,
                base_seed=42,
                max_batches=10,
                fixed_config=diagnostic_config
            )
            self.view.model.eval()
            with torch.no_grad():
                measure_nonpadding_embedding_alignment(self.view.item_emb)
                for batch in panel:
                    # Each example has a preceding prefix, original target,
                    # fixed negative, original eligibility and aligned times.
                    reference = evaluate_final_features_and_fixed_pairs(batch)
                    record_intact_margin_statistics(reference)
                    for condition in diagnostic_config.conditions:
                        for seed in [42, 43, 44, 45, 46]:
                            variant = load_persisted_perturbation(batch, condition, seed)
                            if not variant.supported:
                                record_unavailable(condition, variant.reason)
                                continue
                            measured = evaluate_final_features_and_fixed_pairs(
                                variant, targets=batch.targets,
                                negatives=batch.negatives
                            )
                            record_user_paired_effects(
                                reference, measured, variant.eligibility,
                                displacement=variant.displacement,
                                swap_statistics=variant.swap_statistics
                            )
                metrics = aggregate_draws_then_users_then_equal_weight_datasets()
                metrics.update(user_cluster_intervals_if_supported())
                return {
                    'metrics': metrics,
                    'metric_definitions': definitions_with_counts_scope_and_limits()
                }
        finally:
            restore_all_rng_states_and_per_module_modes(state)


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return grounded_prompt(
        metrics=raw_diagnosis['metrics'],
        definitions=raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        required_fields=['status', 'core_findings', 'key_implications', 'evidence'],
        constraints=[
            'Use measured quantities and explicitly report unavailable evidence.',
            'Training sensitivity is neither validation accuracy nor causal preference.',
            'Do not infer ownership, satisfaction, compatibility or simulator traits.'
        ]
    )

originality.positive: Combines architecture-aware inference, fixed-target perturbations, training-state isolation and explicit missing-data semantics in a reusable diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: The controls and measurements are established techniques; the contribution remains disciplined integration rather than a new recommendation algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Provides reproducible hypotheses for later pooling, recency and objective interventions across all four categories.
future_potential.negative: Sensitivity may not predict pinned validation HR@10, and repeated calibration against the same validation users can overfit model selection.

code_difficulty.positive: The core panel and fixed-pair scoring reuse existing model hooks and require no external data, pretrained weights or new training objective.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct RNG isolation, prefix alignment, timestamp-constrained swaps, masked-hole controls and checkpoint-level aggregation require considerably more work than the original rating implied.

related_work.title: Oh and Cho (2024), recency-bias study [1]
contributions: The supplied research summary describes a recency-bias metric and performance gains from mitigating excessive recent-item emphasis.
Motivates separate measurements of recent-history and older-history dependence.
limitations: Does not establish the appropriate recency weighting for these four datasets or validate the proposed adapter.
Greater sensitivity to recent interactions is not inherently an improvement.

related_work.title: Liu et al., RecSys 2025, constrained history shuffling [2]
contributions: The supplied summary identifies item-availability confounding in random history shuffling.
The supplied author-code description specifies modified Fisher–Yates swaps using training-first-observation constraints, fixed timestamp slots and frozen minimum-timestamp occurrences.
limitations: Constrained shuffling measures model sensitivity rather than causal user preferences.
Training first observations approximate availability; frozen events, repeats and restricted partners preserve residual order.
The routine does not establish uniform sampling over feasible permutations, and window-restricted shuffling differs from the released complete-history intervention.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle, On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation [3]
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can produce model comparisons that disagree with full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not replace the task's pinned sampled validation objective or establish a relationship between training sensitivity and recommendation accuracy.

related_work.title: Original SASRec implementation: model, sampler and attention [4]
contributions: Documents right-aligned histories, left-padding, absolute array-slot positional embeddings, causal attention and final-slot inference.
The sampler aligns each input interaction with its immediate successor and ignores zero targets.
limitations: The actual RecHarness architecture and compatibility hooks must still be checked against these conventions.
Deletion with compaction changes surviving absolute positions; arbitrary masked-hole support cannot be assumed.

related_work.title: PyTorch DataLoader documentation [5]
contributions: Documents generator-controlled sampling and worker seeds, including iterator-related RNG consumption.
Supports using separate diagnostic data loading and generators to avoid changing the training stream.
limitations: Restoring parent RNG states cannot rewind worker-local state or prefetched batches.
Torch RNG isolation alone does not restore Python, NumPy or independently owned generator states.

related_work.title: Liu et al., released constrained-shuffling implementation
contributions: Provides the swap feasibility inequalities, chronological scan, frozen first-occurrence handling and preservation of repeated occurrences.
Supplies implementation details needed to distinguish faithful reproduction from a model-window adaptation.
limitations: According to the supplied inspection, its seed argument does not initialize the global Python randomness used by the shuffle.
Its complete-history intervention supplies no special treatment for truncated model windows.

related_work.title: Woolridge et al., training-history perturbation study
contributions: The supplied summary describes shuffled training histories with held-out validation and test targets preserved.
Helps distinguish training-data interventions from frozen-model, fixed-target diagnostic perturbations.
limitations: Results from retraining on altered histories do not directly validate inference-only sensitivity measurements.

related_work.title: Scikit-learn, nested versus non-nested model selection guidance
contributions: Explains optimistic bias when the same evaluation outcomes support both tuning and assessment.
Motivates freezing diagnostic thresholds before benchmark validation or labeling their analysis exploratory.
limitations: The example is general model-selection guidance rather than a sequential-recommendation experiment.
It does not authorize changing the task's official splits or host evaluator.
